Details
Update: January 2026

The Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard (LCHS) Version 4 incorporates updates to improve clarity, simplify processes, and reflect lessons learned from Version 3 and stakeholder feedback. These updates are:

expanded eligibility requirements for biomethane supply, now allowing sourcing via the gas grid under a mass balance approach
simplified material classification process for Refinery Off Gas
new process for evidencing Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin (REGOs), aligning with wider energy sector practices
introduction of asphalt as an additional solid carbon permissible end use and clarification of requirements for gas splitting production pathways
addition of a new section on stored feedstocks and fuels to clarify requirements for producers
updated emissions factors, technical parameters and calculation methodologies in the Data Annex
restructured guidance and updated terminology throughout for improved clarity
new versions of Hydrogen Emissions Calculators (HEC) which reflect updated pathways and data

See the full update notice on page 6 of the main LCHS Standard document.

The Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard (LCHS) outlines a methodology for calculating lifecycle emissions from hydrogen production and sets compliance requirements, including a Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions threshold, for hydrogen to be defined as ‘low carbon’. The LCHS aims to ensure that government-supported hydrogen production directly contributes to achieving our carbon reduction targets.

Hydrogen producers in the UK seeking to claim their hydrogen as ‘low carbon’, including for eligibility for government schemes, need to demonstrate that they have followed the LCHS and complied with its requirements.

The LCHS places requirements on hydrogen producers, including for them to:

calculate and report their GHG emissions up to the ‘point of production’ by following the prescribed methodology
produce hydrogen that meets a GHG emission intensity of 20g CO2e/MJLHV or less
employ an eligible hydrogen production pathway
set out a risk mitigation plan for fugitive hydrogen emissions and produce an annual report on these fugitive emissions
meet additional requirements for the use of biogenic inputs, where relevant and as appropriate for the biogenic material’s source and classification
meet the conditions of Standard Compliance as applicable to their production pathway
have a Data Collection and Monitoring Procedure in place with the relevant Delivery Partner for the corresponding scheme applying the Standard

We expect to continue to review and update the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard, to ensure it remains fit for purpose and keeps pace with the growing hydrogen economy.

Data annex to the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard

The data annex provides data and other useful information needed to determine compliance with the GHG Emissions Intensity Threshold and other requirements within the LCHS. 

The data annex is reviewed and updated on a regular basis to incorporate new industry practices, respond to changes in referenced datasets, and adopt more accurate or up-to-date sources of information.

Previous versions of the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard

Projects receiving government support should use the version of the LCHS mentioned in their specific agreement. 

You can access previous versions in the zipped files under Documents.

Hydrogen Emissions Calculator

The calculator has been updated for use with the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard, Version 4, January 2026.

The Hydrogen Emissions Calculator (HEC) should be used to calculate the GHG emissions associated with a prospective hydrogen production facility to determine its likely compliance with the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard.

For government schemes and policies applying the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard, the appropriate scheme guidance will confirm whether they need to use the calculator, and if necessary, how it should be used.

There are 2 versions of the calculator:

For electrolytic projects - this streamlined version can accommodate data related to typical electrolytic hydrogen production processes (covering all types of electricity sources).

The full version - this accommodates data related to any current eligible hydrogen production pathways as detailed in the LCHS.

Note that electrolytic projects using biogenic inputs to generate electricity must use the full version.
